title: Optimistic decode gate with confidence venting and degraded paths
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Add an optimistic (speculative) decode gate that trials faster/cheaper decode paths for incoming prefill+decode requests, emits a compact confidence signal ("confidence venting") early in decoding, and implements deterministic degraded paths when acceptance falls below thresholds. This ticket focuses on the runtime integration: kernel-aware trialing, attention optimization toggles during trials, scheduling windows for prefill vs decode, metrics for acceptance and rollback triggers, and a phased rollout plan.

Motivation: We want to reduce end-to-end token cost and p99 latency for common queries by opportunistically running a low-cost decode path in parallel to the primary path or as a fast-path single-token probe. To avoid user-visible regressions, we need a lightweight early acceptance signal and robust fallback/degrade rules tied to quantifiable metrics.

Non-goals: Model selection policy for product tiering, UI changes in Console, or cross-region routing logic (handled in separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a 'trial' API mode that can be enabled per-route via flag
Trial path can bind to an alternative kernel profile (e.g., fused-attn-fast, int8-quant) with explicit kernel selector hint
A compact numeric confidence signal (0.0-1.0) is produced within the first 4 decode tokens from the trial path and logged to telemetry
If confidence < threshold for configured consecutive probes, primary path is used for full output and trial results are discarded
Graceful degrade paths implemented: reduce beam/length, switch to quantized variant, or route to dedicated capacity depending on policy
End-to-end unit tests + e2e canary show no >0.5% increase in top-line rejection rate and no >5% regression in output quality on the canonical eval set
Observability: dashboards for trial acceptance rate, probe latency, rollback count, and cost delta per-model
Feature gate + canary rollout with automatic rollback on thresholded SLA regressions
design_notes:
Key ideas: 1) Kernel-aware trialing: add lightweight kernel hint to trial requests so the runtime schedules a variant of the model using smaller memory/kernels (e.g., 8-bit kernels, reduced attention window). 2) Attention gating: trial path uses attention downsampling (strided attention or local window) for first N tokens; primary path uses full attention. 3) Confidence venting: trial decoder returns a compact acceptance signature composed of token-level logit margin statistics and a calibrated probability; this lives alongside existing telemetry as a numeric field 'trial_confidence'. 4) Scheduling: prefill and trial decode should be co-scheduled when prefill latency budget allows — otherwise trial should be single-token probe after prefill. 5) Fallbacks: define ordered degraded actions (1. resume primary decode, 2. re-run with full kernels, 3. escalate to dedicated pool) depending on severity.

Trade-offs considered: emitting confidence early reduces blind fallbacks but adds coupling between trial and primary; to minimize coupling the primary never consumes trial KV directly, only a compact acceptance signal. We considered speculative fusion (materialize trial outputs into primary) but rejected for safety and cache complexity.

Open questions: calibration schedule for confidence thresholds (static vs telemetry-driven), policies for multi-tenant vs dedicated customers, and how to account for token-level hallucination signals into the confidence venting metric.
implementation_plan: API: add 'trial_mode' boolean and 'kernel_hint' string to runtime request proto (backwards compatible)
Runtime: implement TrialScheduler that launches trial worker with pinned kernel profile and limited KV cache size
Attention: implement opt-in attention downsample strategy for trial kernels (configurable ratio)
Safety: add deterministic discard path so trial outputs are never used unless acceptance==true
Tests: unit tests for kernel hint glue, attention downsample correctness, and simulated mismatch fallbacks
Canary: roll to internal customers on runtime-1.22-canary with feature flag, monitor for 72 hours, then broader rollout
telemetry_plan: Create dashboards and alerts: 1) Trial acceptance rate (by model, route, kernel_hint), 2) Early confidence distribution histograms, 3) Trial vs primary latency and p99 tail deltas, 4) Cost savings estimate per-100k tokens, 5) Rollback rate and root-cause tagging. Alert rules: rollback_rate > 1% over 5m OR p99 latency regression > 10% triggers automatic rollback. Add sampling traces linking trial request id to primary request id for debug.
qa_and_tests: Unit tests for new proto fields and kernel selection logic; integration tests that simulate kernel mismatch and ensure safe discard behavior; synthetic traffic replay comparing baseline vs trial enabled; quality regression tests against canonical prompt set (automatic A/B). Include adversarial prompt set to validate worst-case fallback behavior.
rollout_and_rollback: Feature gated by route flag. Phase 1: internal canary (5% of internal traffic), Phase 2: whitelisted customers (opt-in), Phase 3: 25% gradual ramp with automated monitors, Phase 4: global. Rollback if any of the following: 1) trial_rollback_rate exceeds 2% and corresponds to quality regression on eval set, 2) p99 latency increases beyond configured SLO window, 3) cost-savings negative for >24h. Rollback plan: flip feature flag, purge trial workers from scheduler, and invalidate trial metrics to reduce noise.
security_and_compliance: Trial mode does not persist trial KV to disk. Trial logs marked redact-level=high by default. No customer data leaves region. Security review not required for initial implementation but will be re-evaluated for private deployments.
